sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: POTENT NV SHORTWAVE TROUGH EXPECTED TO CONTINUE ESE TO THE FOUR CORNERS REGION THIS EVE BEFORE TURNING SLIGHTLY N OF E AND REACHING THE CNTRL HIGH PLNS EARLY MON. FAST WNW FLOW ACROSS THE E PACIFIC SUGGESTS THAT THE SYSTEM SHOULD REMAIN PROGRESSIVE DESPITE SOME TENDENCY TO FURTHER AMPLIFY/CLOSE-OFF AS IT ENCOUNTERS MORE SLOWLY-PROGRESSIVE RIDGE OVER THE CNTRL U.S. COLD FRONT ATTENDANT TO THE TROUGH...NOW OVER CNTRL UT/NW AZ...WILL SWEEP E/SE ACROSS THE SRN PLATEAU TODAY...WITH THE MOST RAPID ADVANCE EXPECTED OVER NE AZ...NW NM...AND SRN CO. AT THE SAME TIME...DOWNSTREAM LEE TROUGH OVER THE CNTRL/NRN HIGH PLNS SHOULD STRENGTHEN AND REACH FAR WRN KS...WRN NEB...AND THE WRN DAKOTAS BY THE END OF THE PERIOD AS LEE CYCLONE EVOLVES OVER NE CO/THE NEB PANHANDLE. COLD FRONT WITH THE NV TROUGH...AND AREA OF ASCENT TO ITS EAST...SHOULD BE THE MAIN FOCI FOR ORGANIZED STRONG TO SVR TSTMS OVER THE LWR 48 TODAY. OTHERWISE...SCTD TSTMS LIKELY WILL PERSIST INVOF STALLING FRONT OVER THE NRN GULF OF MEXICO...SRN GA...AND FL AS ASSOCIATED UPR TROUGH DEPARTS THE NERN U.S.

sections.title: FOUR CORNERS REGION THIS AFTN/EVE
sections.text: A BAND OF STRONG ASCENT/MID-LVL COOLING WILL CROSS THE FOUR CORNERS REGION TODAY IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF NV SHORTWAVE TROUGH. COUPLED WITH LIKELIHOOD FOR APPRECIABLE SFC HEATING...SETUP APPEARS FAVORABLE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF FAIRLY NUMEROUS TSTMS BY EARLY AFTN FROM NE AZ AND SE UT INTO NW NM/SW CO. WITH TIME...MORE ISOLD ACTIVITY MAY EXTEND SWD INTO W CNTRL AND SW NM. WHILE RELATIVELY LIMITED BY CNTRL/ERN U.S. STANDARDS...SUFFICIENT MOISTURE /PW AOA .75 INCHES/ WILL BE PRESENT FOR STORMS GIVEN STRONG UPR-LVL FORCING FOR ASCENT AND LOW-LVL UPLIFT PROVIDED BY COLD FRONT/TERRAIN. PLUME OF SOMEWHAT MORE SUBSTANTIAL MOISTURE NOW OVER SE AZ...PER GPS AND COMPOSITE SATELLITE DATA...MAY SPREAD FAR ENOUGH NE BY LATER IN THE DAY TO ENHANCE STORM POTENTIAL/LONGEVITY OVER NE AZ/NW NM. WITH AMPLE DEEP SHEAR FOR ORGANIZED/SUSTAINED UPDRAFTS PROVIDED BY BELT OF 40-50 KT WSW FLOW ROUNDING BASE OF THE UPR TROUGH...STORMS LIKELY WILL ORGANIZE INTO BANDS/SMALL CLUSTERS. A FEW SUPERCELLS MAY OCCUR...ESPECIALLY OVER SE HALF OF OUTLOOKED AREA...WHERE MOISTURE AVAILABILITY/HEATING/DEEP SHEAR SHOULD BE GREATEST. THESE STORMS MAY PRODUCE LOCALLY DMGG WIND...HAIL...AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO. A POTENTIAL A

sections.title: FOUR CORNERS REGION/SRN-CENTRAL ROCKIES SWD TO SERN AZ/SWRN NM
sections.text: FORECAST REMAINS ON TRACK ACROSS THE FOUR CORNERS REGION...WITH THE ONLY EXCEPTION BEING TO EXTEND THE 5 PERCENT THREATS FOR HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS INTO MORE OF SERN AZ/SWRN NM. LIGHTNING DATA/RADAR IMAGERY SHOWED STORMS HAVE DEVELOPED WITHIN THE SRN EXTENT OF THE POTENT SHORTWAVE TROUGH TRACKING EWD INTO THE FOUR CORNERS/SRN ROCKIES AREA. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 25-35 KT WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS...WITH MARGINAL INSTABILITY AND WEAKER FORCING OVER SERN AZ/SWRN NM TENDING TO LIMIT OVERALL COVERAGE. OTHERWISE...STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL REMAIN A THREAT FROM PARTS OF ERN/SERN UT...NERN AZ INTO WRN/CENTRAL CO AND NWRN/NRN NM THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING.

sections.title: SRN AND NRN ATLANTIC COASTAL AREAS
sections.text: PART OF THE SRN ATLANTIC COASTAL AREA /FROM ERN SC TO ADJACENT GA/ HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM GENERAL THUNDER WITH THIS OUTLOOK ISSUANCE... AS LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE AND THE SRN EXTENT OF THE ERN LONGWAVE TROUGH HAVE MOVED EAST OF THIS REGION. MEANWHILE...FARTHER N...LOW LEVEL WIND SHIFT AND THREAT FOR TSTMS HAVE SHIFTED OFF THE COAST OF NEW ENGLAND. ..PETERS.. 09/22/2013 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1115 AM CDT SUN SEP 22 2013/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR AN INCREASE SEVERE STORM THREAT WHICH PROBABLY WILL REQUIRE ONE OR MORE WATCHES WITHIN THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS OR SO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A VIGOROUS MID/UPPER TROUGH WILL CONTINUE TO STEADILY SHIFT EAST OF THE GREAT BASIN AND LOWER COLORADO VALLEY THROUGH THE LATE MORNING AND EARLY AFTERNOON HOURS. ALTHOUGH THE ENVIRONMENT AHEAD OF IT IS NOT ESPECIALLY MOIST...MOISTURE IS INCREASING...AND APPEARS SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT MODEST CAPE WITH FURTHER INSOLATION. STRONG LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION IS ALREADY CONTRIBUTING TO CONSIDERABLE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT EAST OF THE WASATCH INTO WESTERN COLORADO...AND STORMS APPEAR LIKELY TO INCREASE SOUTHWARD THROUGH THE COLORADO PLATEAU DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. DEEP LAYER MEAN FLOW AND SHEAR ASSOCIATED WITH A 50-70 KT 500 MB JET STREAK ARE ALREADY FAVORABLE FOR ORGANIZED CONVECTION...INCLUDING SUPERCELLS...ACROSS THIS REGION. AS BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION PROGRESSES...A SUBSTANTIVE INCREASE IN SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL APPEARS PROBABLE...POSSIBLY AS EARLY AS THE 18-19Z TIME FRAME.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: RISK FOR SEVERE HAIL/LOCALIZED SEVERE WIND GUSTS CONTINUES ACROSS THE WW AREAS. DAMAGING WIND POTENTIAL MAY INCREASE BY 22-23Z...AND TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR THE POSSIBILITY OF AN INCREASING SEVERE WEATHER THREAT WHICH COULD REQUIRE AN ADDITIONAL WATCH ACROSS PARTS OF COLORADO TO THE EAST OF WW 532.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: NUMEROUS...DISCRETE THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING ACROSS THE REGION IN THE PRESENCE OF 35-50+ KT SOUTHWESTERLY DEEP LAYER MEAN FLOW...WITH STRONG SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS. STRONGEST CELLS ARE ROOTED IN AN UNSTABLE BOUNDARY LAYER LAYER...WHICH WILL CONTINUE TO DESTABILIZE WITH ADDITIONAL INSOLATION THIS AFTERNOON ...PARTICULARLY ACROSS THE PLATEAU REGION OF NORTHEASTERN ARIZONA INTO NORTHWESTERN NEW MEXICO. A MID-LEVEL LOW CENTER...NOW NEAR MILFORD UT...APPEARS TO BE DEVELOPING WITHIN THE VIGOROUS UPSTREAM SHORT WAVE TROUGH...WITH AN AREA OF 60-90 METER 500 MB HEIGHT FALLS LIKELY TO OVERSPREAD MUCH OF THE CURRENT WATCH AREAS BETWEEN NOW AND 23/00Z. WDSS MESH DATA HAS INDICATED THE PRESENCE OF SEVERE HAIL IN THE STRONGER CELLS...WHICH CONTINUE TO INTENSIFY. SOME OF THIS ACTIVITY MAY BEGIN TO CONSOLIDATE INTO A SQUALL LINE ON THE LEADING EDGE OF STRONGER MID-LEVEL FORCING DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS...ACCOMPANIED BY INCREASING POTENTIAL FOR STRONG WIND GUSTS AS IT APPROACHES THE CONTINENTAL DIVIDE. ..KERR.. 09/22/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTM COVERAGE IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE ACROSS THE CNTRL PLAINS NWD INTO WRN SD DURING THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. A FEW OF THESE STORMS MAY BE SEVERE WITH DAMAGING WINDS AS THE PRIMARY THREAT. UNCERTAINTY ON SVR COVERAGE PRECLUDES HIGHER WATCH PROBABILITIES BUT TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED THROUGHOUT THE REGION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY HAS SHOWN AN INCREASINGLY AGITATED CU FIELD FROM FAR NE CO NWD INTO WRN SD. REGIONAL RADARS HAVE ALSO RECENTLY SHOWN SCATTERED ECHOES IN THIS SAME AREA. THIS LEADS CONFIDENCE TO THE SCENARIO DEPICTED BY RECENT HRRR RUNS...WHICH PROGS GRADUALLY INCREASING TSTM COVERAGE AS HEIGHT FALLS CONTINUE ACROSS THE REGION OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. RECENT SURFACE ANALYSIS PLACES A LOW OVER THE FAR WRN ND/SD BORDER WITH A LEE TROUGH EXTENDING SWD ACROSS WRN SD AND WRN NEB/NEB PANHANDLE TO ANOTHER LOW OVER NE CO. CONVERGENCE ALONG THIS LEE TROUGH WILL LIKELY INCREASE AS THE PREVIOUSLY MENTIONED LARGE SCALE HEIGHT FALLS CONTINUE AND THE TROUGH SHARPENS. THIS FACTOR ALSO INCREASES CONFIDENCE IN THE HRRR FORECAST SCENARIO. MAIN LIMITING FACTOR IS LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE. CURRENT SURFACE OBSERVATIONS REVEAL DEWPOINTS ARE GENERALLY IN THE LOW 50S E OF THE LEE TROUGH. THIS MIXING HAS RESULTED IN VERY STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES /GREATER THAN 9 DEG C PER KM/ BUT ALSO LIMITED INSTABILITY. CURRENT MESOANALYSIS PLACES MLCAPE FROM 500 TO 1000 J/KG. WHILE CONFIDENCE IN SVR STORM COVERAGE IS LOW...INCREASING TSTM ACTIVITY WITHIN THIS ENVIRONMENT MAY YIELD A FEW SVR STORMS AND TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED CLOSELY. PRIMARY SVR THREAT IS DAMAGING WINDS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS MUCH OF NRN/CNTRL NM INTO SCNTRL CO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONGEST MID LEVEL FORCING APPEARS TO BE SPREADING ACROSS SWRN CO/NWRN NM ATTM...PER LAGGING BAND OF FORCED CONVECTION THAT STRETCHES FROM ARCHULETA COUNTY CO...SWWD INTO MCKINELY COUNTY NM. NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS ARE NOTED ACROSS THE RIO GRANDE RIVER VALLEY INTO THE WRN UPSLOPE REGIONS OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS. LATEST THINKING IS CONVECTION WILL REMAIN MOST ROBUST ACROSS THIS REGION AS ANY STORMS THAT SHIFT EAST OF THE HIGHER TERRAIN WILL ENCOUNTER SOMEWHAT DRIER AND MORE SUBSIDENT AIR MASS OVER THE PLAINS. HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS REMAIN POSSIBLE WITH CONVECTION ACROSS THE SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH REGION. ..DARROW.. 09/22/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
